title: HABC/2/2021 of AMAN TALWAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Habeas Corpus Petition No. 2 of 2021
Aman Talwar ...Petitioner
Versus

State of Uttarakhand and others ...Respondents
Present:-
Mr. Siddharth Bankoti, Advocate, holding brief of Mr.
Vipul Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner
Mr. Lalit Miglani, A.G.A. for the State.
Mr. Shakti Singh, Advocate for the private respondents.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Present habeas corpus petition has been filed by the
petitioner seeking custody of his son, who was born on
07.10.2010 and staying with his mother, the respondent no.5.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused
the record.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that he was staying in
live-in-relationship with the respondent no.5 from the year
2008 up till December, 2020. A child was born out of the
relationship. The petitioner had taken great care of his son.
But, on 23.12.2020, the respondent no.5 left the company of
the petitioner and started staying in Delhi. The petitioner
claims that he is natural guardian of the child in view of
Section 6A of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956
(para 15 of the petition- although it is section 6 (a) and not A).

2
4. The respondent no.5 has filed counter affidavit.
According to her, the petitioner established physical relations
with her under the pretext of marriage, but did not perform
marriage ever. She filed an FIR under Sections 376, 328 and
506 IPC against the petitioner at Police Station Wazirabad,
Delhi. According to her, the child was born out from their
relationship. On 25.12.2020, it is the petitioner, who
dropped the respondent no.5 and her son at Delhi. He
misbehaved with her and then police was called.
5. During the course of hearing, on 11.08.2021, on
behalf of the petitioner, it was argued that the child is living
with mother but atrocities were being committed on him. The
Court sought a report from the State. The report was
submitted, but it revealed that the Police Officer
telephonically inquired from the respondent no.5 about the
well being of the child. Therefore, the Court further directed
the State to get the proper report.
6. Now, the report is placed before the Court, during
the course of hearing, by the learned State counsel which
reveals that a Police Sub-Inspector had visited the place of
stay of the respondent no.5. The Police Officer has reported
that the respondent no.5 does not misbehave with her son.
He is being looked after very well. He is admitted in a very
good school. In fact, in his own handwriting, the corpus has

3
written that he is staying with his mother, who takes his care
very much and he wants to stay with her mother. As stated,
it has been endorsed by the Police Officer.
7. Learned counsel for the petitioner would submit
that the petitioner is natural guardian of his son. He needs
custody of him. According to him, the welfare of the child is
paramount consideration.
8. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State
would submit that the child is staying with her mother. He is
looked after well. It is also argued that the petitioner is also
trying to misuse the Government machinery by way of filing
the instant petition.
9. Learned counsel for the respondent no.5 would
also submit that the respondent no.5 is looking after her son
very well. He is under her care, going to school and growing
well.
10. It is a habeas corpus petition. Basically, if a
person is detained illegally and without any reason, the
Court may direct for production of the corpus before it. Here
in the instant case, it is the case of the petitioner that he was
in live-in-relationship the corpus was born, who is living with

4
his mother. The corpus was born in the year 2010. Now, the
petitioner is filed in the year 2021. According to the
petitioner, in the year 2020, the respondent no.5 had taken
the corpus out from his custody. It is the petitioner, in fact,
who had dropped the respondent no.5 and the corpus in
Delhi. The dispute relates to the custody of a child.
11. Apparently, this Court does not see any reason to
exercise the jurisdiction under Article 226 of the Constitution
of India for production of corpus before the Court. The
corpus is well with his mother. The Police Officer reports that
he is being taken well care by his mother. The respondent
no.5, the mother states that she is looking after her child
very well. Therefore, if the petitioner is aggrieved by the
custody of child with his mother, he may file a custody suit
as permissible under the law.
12. A kind of similar issue was discussed by the
Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Nithya Anand
Raghavan State (NCT of Delhi) and another, (2017) 8 SCC
454 and in para 47, the Hon'ble Supreme Court observed as
hereunder:-
"47. In a habeas corpus petition as aforesaid, the
High Court must examine at the threshold whether the
minor is in lawful or unlawful custody of another person
(private respondent named in the writ petition). For
considering that issue, in a case such as the present

5
one, it is enough to note that the private respondent was
none other than the natural guardian of the minor being
her biological mother. Once that fact is ascertained, it
can be presumed that the custody of the minor with
his/her mother is lawful. In such a case, only in
exceptionable situation, the custody of the minor (girl
child) may be ordered to be taken away from her mother
for being given to any other person including the
husband (father of the child), in exercise of writ
jurisdiction. Instead, the other parent can be asked to
resort to a substantive prescribed remedy for getting
custody of the child."
13. In the instant case also, the corpus is with his
mother. There is dispute with regard to the custody.
14. Having considered the entirety of facts, this Court
is of the view that this petition deserves to be dismissed.
15. The petition is dismissed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 29.06.2022
Jitendra
